s1.syndrome_frame: Acute encephalopathy with seizures and cerebral edema following synthetic cannabis use
salient_findings: Diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema on MRI
History of synthetic cannabis use prior to seizure
key_facts: Presented to emergency department after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure
History of left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago
Used synthetic cannabis with resolution of symptoms and neurologic deficits 4 months ago
Used synthetic cannabis just before the seizure
Normal complete blood cell count, chemistry panel, aspirin level, acetaminophen level, alcohol level, and liver function tests
Urine drug screen positive for cannabinoids

per_call: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis due to Measles

shortlist.label: Synthetic Cannabinoid–Induced Toxic Encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of synthetic cannabis use and presentation with seizures and cerebral edema

shortlist.label: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of seizures, cerebral edema, and history of synthetic cannabis use are consistent with PRES

shortlist.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS)
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of synthetic cannabis use and presentation with seizures and cerebral edema are consistent with RCVS

shortlist.label: Post-Stroke Seizure Disorder (Epilepsy)
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of left cerebral ischemic stroke and presentation with seizures

shortlist.label: Toxic Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of seizures, cerebral edema, and history of synthetic cannabis use are consistent with toxic leukoencephalopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's recent use of synthetic cannabis before the seizure and history of similar symptoms after using synthetic cannabis 4 months ago, along with the presence of diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Post-Stroke Seizure Disorder (Epilepsy)
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of stroke, the temporal relationship between synthetic cannabis use and seizures suggests a more direct cause.

rejected.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS)
rejected.why: RCVS typically presents with thunderclap headache, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
rejected.why: PRES is often associated with hypertension, eclampsia, or immunosuppression, which are not indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Toxic Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: While this condition could be considered due to the patient's history of substance use, the acute presentation and direct temporal relationship with synthetic cannabis use point more towards an acute toxic encephalopathy rather than a leukoencephalopathy, which typically implies more chronic changes.
